summary: Kickoff for Redwood onboarding with Lattice Health. Customer aims to run a 4-week pilot on dedicated capacity to support inference for internal search and clinical summarization. Discussed SSO (SAML), VPC peering, SOC2 controls, KMS integration, and expected latency/cost tradeoffs. Agreed action items to exchange docs and schedule a technical benchmark session.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Lattice Head of MLOps), Nora (Platform Eng), Samir (CTO)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have a packed 40 minutes. quick intros?
[00:08] Ethan Park: Yep, Ethan here, head of MLOps at Lattice, I run infra and the inference pipelines.
[00:14] Nora Singh: Nora, platform eng, I’ll own the VPC peering and firewall side.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Samir, CTO, I’ll be around for architecture and budget decisions.
[00:23] Maya Chen: Awesome. From Redwood we have Diego who will lead integration, and Priya who’ll be your CSM. Diego?
[00:29] Diego Ramos: Hi all. Quick agenda: onboarding timeline, infra requirements (VPC/SSO/KMS), pilot options (dedicated vs hosted), benchmarks and next steps.

[00:45] Nora: Sounds good. Our goal is to have a pilot running in dedicated capacity by mid-April, about 2-4 models, mostly open models, and we need SOC2 level controls.
[00:55] Priya Kapoor: Great — SOC2 is familiar, we have SOC2 Type II docs and can share redacted reports. Also we can walk through SSO/SAML setup.

[01:10] Diego: For the dedicated trial we’ll provision a small dedicated GPU pool. That gives stable throughput and isolation, which helps when you’re sensitive about data residency. If you want, we can start with hosted API while we set up VPC peering so you don’t wait.
[01:28] Ethan: Hmm, latency is important for the clinical summarization use case — <0.5s per token ideally — but cost is also a factor. How predictable is performance on dedicated?
[01:38] Diego: Dedicated gives the most predictable p99 latency because you’re not sharing capacity. We’ll also tune batching and KV cache. We recommend profiling your sequence lengths; if most requests are short we can optimize kernels for that.

[01:55] Samir: On security, we need KMS integration and audit logs. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:03] Maya: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and for Dedicated we can integrate with customer-managed KMS in most cloud setups. We’ll share the KMS implementation guide. Audit logs and the console expose per-request tracing for compliance.

[02:20] Nora: About networking — we use AWS VPCs and we prefer VPC peering or privatelink. What does Redwood require?
[02:28] Diego: We support both. For Private deployment it’s within your VPC. For Dedicated we do VPC peering and provide recommended CIDR ranges and firewall rules. I’ll send the exact list.

[02:45] Ethan: Any known gotchas around NATs, proxies, or egress rules?
[02:51] Diego: Mostly time sync and MTU issues show up; also some corporate proxies rewrite TLS. We’ll include a checklist. The healthcheck endpoint and mutual TLS can help.

[03:10] Priya: Timeline-wise, if Nora can send VPC CIDR and SAML metadata this week we can provision trial infra next week and schedule a benchmarks deep dive the week after.

[03:25] Nora: I can get the CIDR and firewall rules by Friday, and I’ll pull SAML metadata from our IdP.

[03:33] Samir: Cost question — are you recommending quantized models or smaller model variants for the pilot? We don’t want to lose quality on clinical text.
[03:41] Diego: For initial pilot we usually recommend attempting a quantized variant (int8) where quality impact is minimal. Redwood Optimize can propose quantization profiles per workload and we can A/B test quality. If quality is critical, pin to full-fp model for the first benchmark then try quantized later.

[04:05] Ethan: Good to know. Also curious about model management: version pinning and rollouts — we need stable behavior for production.
[04:12] Maya: The platform supports model version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to compatible variants. We’ll show that in the console demo.

[04:26] Priya: Quick note on governance — we can enable audit retention policies and long-term logs if you need them for audits.

[04:38] Nora: Do you have SOC2 and ISO?
[04:41] Maya: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 coverage. I’ll attach the certification and the redacted report.

[05:00] Diego: For the pilot benchmarks, what are the success criteria? Latency per request, cost per 1M tokens, and quality pass rate on our prompt set?
[05:10] Ethan: Right: 95th percentile latency under 700ms for our interactive flows, cost under $X per 1M tokens — Samir will confirm the exact budget — and no more than 3% dropped quality on our eval prompts.

[05:26] Samir: I’ll send the budget target later today.

[05:33] Maya: Great. On integrations we’ll provide a sample container and an API key rotation schedule. Diego, anything on tracing?

[05:40] Diego: We have tracing hooks for per-request token cost and latency. We can send a sample dashboard for token-level breakdowns and per-model metrics.

[06:00] Ethan: One more thing — do you support private model uploads or do we only pull from the model catalog?

[06:07] Diego: For Private deployments you can load your private models. For Dedicated we support bringing custom models as long as they’re compatible with the runtime; we’ll validate at onboarding.

[06:20] Nora: Network question again — do you need a peering connection initiated on our side or will Redwood initiate?

[06:27] Diego: We usually ask the customer to create a peering request and our infra team accepts it. We’ll send step-by-step.

[06:40] Priya: Ok, to summarize — Nora shares VPC details and SAML metadata; Maya sends SOC2 docs, onboarding guide, and pricing; Diego shares integration repo and benchmarking plan. We’ll reconvene for a deep technical run through week of 03/28.

[06:58] Nora: Sounds good. One more quick Q: Has anyone run into issues with tokenization differences between models affecting billing? We saw odd token counts on another platform.

[07:07] Diego: Tokenization variance happens; we provide token-level cost breakdown and can help normalize prompts or use model-specific tokenization libraries.

[07:20] Ethan: Alright, anything else from Redwood?

[07:23] Maya: Nothing else. Thanks everyone, we’ll follow up via email with the attachments.

[07:30] Samir: Thanks all.

Notes (auto):
- Customer wants 4-week dedicated pilot starting ~mid-April.
- Key asks: SOC2 docs, KMS integration, VPC peering guide, SAML setup, benchmarking.
- Next meeting: technical deep dive / benchmark planning (week of 2027-03-28).

End of transcript (some minor transcription mis-hears are present; proper names may be slightly off)
